steps.say: Ureteroneocystostomy is the reimplantation of the distal ureter into the bladder. It is used for strictures within 4 cm to 5 cm of the bladder entry. The scarred segment is excised and the healthy end is spatulated. A submucosal tunnel is created to prevent reflux. A short healthy ureter is repaired without tension.
steps.tx: **Ureteroneocystostomy** (ureter reimplantation into the bladder, **ureteral reimplantation**) is the repair for distal strictures or cuts within **4 cm to 5 cm** (four to five centimetres) of the ureterovesical junction (bladder entry). Excise the scarred segment, spatulate the healthy end, and tunnel it through bladder muscle to resist reflux, because a short sound ureter reaches without tension.

steps.say: Psoas hitch is used for distal ureteral gaps of 6 cm to 8 cm. The bladder dome is mobilised and fixed to the psoas minor tendon. The lifted bladder is advanced toward the cut ureter. A slack tension free join is achieved. Nonabsorbable sutures are placed into tendon. Muscle bites are avoided as they pull through.
steps.tx: A **psoas hitch** (bladder lift to the muscle) bridges distal gaps of **6 cm to 8 cm** (six to eight centimetres) by mobilising the bladder dome to the **psoas minor** (small loin tendon) and fixing it there. The hitched bladder climbs toward the cut ureter, so the join lies slack. Anchor with nonabsorbable sutures into tendon, not muscle fibres, because muscle pulls through under tension.

steps.say: Boari flap is constructed when defects reach 12 cm to 15 cm. A pedicled bladder strip is rolled into a tubularized flap. The base to apex ratio is maintained at 2:1. Tip necrosis is prevented by a broad base. The bladder donor site is closed in layers. A catheter is left for drainage.
steps.tx: A **Boari flap** (bladder wall tube, **tubularized flap**) replaces mid and lower defects of **12 cm to 15 cm** (twelve to fifteen centimetres) by rolling a pedicled bladder strip into a conduit. Keep the base to apex ratio at **2:1** (two to one) to protect tip blood supply, because a narrow based long flap necroses. Close the bladder donor site in two layers over a catheter.

steps.say: Transureteroureterostomy is performed for long proximal ureteral loss. The injured ureter is swung across the midline. An end to side join is made with the healthy recipient ureter. Only one functioning system is required for drainage. Most injuries are caused during pelvic surgery. The ureteric danger sites are shown in the operative diagram.
steps.tx: **Transureteroureterostomy** (ureter to ureter join, **TUU** (cross body join)) swings the injured donor ureter across the midline in front of the aorta to meet the healthy recipient ureter end to side. It rescues long proximal losses when bladder flaps fall short, because only one functioning recipient system is needed. Most such injuries follow pelvic surgery near the **ureter** (urine tube), so know its danger sites.

steps.say: TUU contraindications are reviewed before any cross body join. Urothelial carcinoma is excluded as it seeds the field. Stone disease and retroperitoneal fibrosis are also bars. Radiated pelvis and bilateral ureteral disease are added cautions. A healthy recipient system is mandatory for success. Bowel interposition is selected when TUU is barred.
steps.tx: The **TUU contraindications** (bars to cross body join) are **urothelial carcinoma** (lining cancer that seeds), chronic stone disease, **retroperitoneal fibrosis** (scarred back wall), prior pelvic radiation, and severe bilateral ureteral disease. Each risks the recipient ureter or the operative field, because TUU sacrifices a healthy system as the drain. Choose bowel interposition or autotransplantation instead when any bar is present.

steps.say: Ileal ureter is reserved for pan ureteral strictures. An isoperistaltic ileal segment is isolated with its blood supply. The distal 15 cm is spared for B12 absorption. Serum creatinine below 2 mg per dL is required before surgery. Failing kidneys are harmed by mucus and acid load. Lifelong surveillance is arranged for stones and tumours.
steps.tx: An **ileal ureter** (bowel tube replacement) uses an **isoperistaltic segment** (gut that propels forward) of terminal ileum while sparing the distal **15 cm** (fifteen centimetres) needed for B12 and bile salts. Reserve it for pan ureteral loss with serum creatinine below **2.0 mg/dL** (safe kidney function), because a failing kidney cannot clear the mucus and acid load that bowel adds.

steps.say: Buccal mucosa graft is used for resistant proximal strictures. A cheek lining patch is harvested and laid as an onlay. The graft is wrapped with vascularised omentum. Free grafts are nourished only by a rich bed. Cheek tissue is known to tolerate urine well. Quilting to the ureteral plate is performed for take.
steps.tx: **Buccal mucosa graft** (cheek lining patch) laid as an onlay and wrapped with vascularised omentum rescues non obliterative proximal and mid strictures that resist endourology. Cheek heals fast and tolerates urine, while the **omental wrap** (fat apron cover) feeds the graft, because free grafts survive only on a rich bed. Harvest a wide graft and quilt it to the ureteral plate.

steps.say: Renal autotransplantation is reserved for extreme ureteral loss. The kidney is moved to the iliac fossa. Vessels are joined to the iliac artery and vein. A short fresh reimplantation is created for drainage. Bladder and bowel options are exhausted first. Vascular complications are watched for carefully after surgery.
steps.tx: **Renal autotransplantation** (self kidney move) shifts the kidney to the **iliac fossa** (lower belly pocket) and joins its vessels to the iliac artery and vein when bladder flaps and bowel are both unusable. It salvages extreme pan ureteral loss with a short fresh ureteroneocystostomy, because the kidney drains beside its new home. Reserve it for last resort, given vascular risk.
